quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm out. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: You should signal to turn ____ before you begin the turn.

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
20 feet
10 feet

questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This warns other drivers of your plans. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices, drive to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation.
Only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep your eyes on the road. Check your mirrors and instrument panel regularly. These habits help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop safely if you can. If you cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: You can help the driver behind you stay a safe distance away by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Driving at a steady speed.

questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance. This helps drivers behind you maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other roads. They also thaw out later than regular pavement. Be careful of ice on bridges even when nearby roads are dry.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first starts to rain.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Oil, rubber, and dirt mix with water when rain first starts. This makes roads very slippery. Slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: When driving up a hill behind a heavy truck, you should know:

options.text: The truck may go slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass. Use caution when approaching large vehicles from behind.

questions.question: What lane space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a recommended driving speed.
The exact speed at which you must travel to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the posted limit if conditions are not ideal. Adjust your speed for rain, snow, or other poor conditions.

questions.question: Are drivers required to use turn signals when leaving a parking space?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Drivers must use their turn signals or hand signals when driving out of a parking space. This helps other drivers know what you are doing and prevents crashes.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that vehicles:

options.text: Driving in both directions may pass.
Next to the broken line may pass.
Next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is showing red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is showing green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or in a curve because you probably won't see oncoming traffic.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or in curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass. Passing is only legal when the road markings allow it and it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close to the vehicle in front of you for better traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Use a low gear before going down steep hills on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Keep a greater distance between you and other vehicles. Avoid sudden stops. Pump the brakes only if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no traffic is coming.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights mean stop. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: Do emotions affect the way we drive?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Strong emotions like anger and fear change how we think and act. These emotions affect the way we drive.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light will come next. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Once the gate is raised, wait to cross the tracks until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: When passing another car, when is it safe to return to the driving lane?

options.text: If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to the driving lane after passing, make sure there is a safe space between your car and the other car. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Tires grip loose gravel and dirt roads less than they grip concrete and asphalt. When driving on gravel or dirt, you must slow down. It takes much longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for drunk drivers.
Curves ahead.
Slippery when wet.
Apply your brakes quickly.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns of low clearance ahead.

questions.question: What do drivers need to drive safely on the interstate?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at increased speeds.
To stay constantly alert.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires drivers to be constantly alert and able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.explanation: This sign (with the arrow) shows where bicycles cross or ride. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles regularly cross or travel next to traffic.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.
